question:

option_2: a bird in hand is worth two in the bush
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. a bird in hand is worth two in the bush.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Bird in hand is worth two in bush" means sure thing is better.

◦ (जो है वही बेहतर)

• The completed sentence reads: He refused the risky new offer and kept his stable job, believing that a bird in hand is worth two in the bush.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. a bird in hand is worth two in the bush.

 

Additional Information

• Option 1: cut to the chase (मुद्दे पर आना): This idiom means get to the point, which does not fit the context of the given sentence.
